text:
tess: kicking off a small sync — we're running a trace-playback experiment to verify parity after the new kernel-selection + batching heuristic landed. focus: KV cache coldstart, determinism with anonymized traces, and measurable perf delta. plan below.
ajay: thanks. which trace slice are we using? full prod day or cohort sample?
tess: cohort sample. we picked the 3% high-latency cohort from last week (anon'd). sampling pipeline produced /traces/anon/2026-03/highlat-3pct.tar.gz. we want apples-to-apples runs against the baseline runtime and the kernel-switch runtime.
maria: for anonymization we removed user IDs and dropped PII fields, left request hashes for matching. seed and cohort labels preserved. double-checked with privacy team.
samir: important: KV warmup differs between runtimes. baseline does synchronous prewarm on first request in a session; new runtime relies on async prefetch and larger batching. we need to control for warmup to avoid false regressions.
tess: agreed. test matrix:
1) baseline kernel + batching (cold start)
2) new kernel-selection + new batching (cold start)
3) baseline with KV-prefill hack (to match new runtime warm state)
4) new runtime forced cold (flush KV between sessions)
Run each with 5 seeds (42..46) and identical trace slice.
noah: we'll use benchbot to orchestrate parallel runs and record per-request latencies, token throughput, and KV hit ratios.
benchbot: enqueueing experiment job id=exp-20260317-01, 20 partitions, seed range 42-46. will post artifacts to /bench/exp-20260317-01/.
ci-bot: note: the CI runner image has the new kernels compiled with AVX-fallback; ensure the hardware tags match when comparing.
ajay: how are we verifying determinism? exact output equality or statistical parity?
maria: two levels: (A) byte-for-byte output equality for deterministic ops (sampling fixed) using seed control and identical kernel flags; (B) token-level distribution checks for generation outputs where non-determinism is expected (compare top-k histograms and perplexity delta).
samir: also log the KV cache sequences per session: prefix hits, cache fill timings, eviction counts. that helped us diagnose the last regression.
tess: good call. here's the playback command to run locally:
```
./playback --trace /traces/anon/highlat-3pct/part-000 --sample-seed 42 --kernels selector=v2 --batching heuristic=cohort-aware --kv-prefill=false --out /tmp/playback-42.json
```
noah: for parity diffs we'll run a small checker that compares response IDs, token counts, and a bloom-filtered sequence signature (to avoid storing outputs with content). sample checker output format below.
maria: example checker output (synthetic):
```
PARITY_REPORT runA=baseline runB=kernel-v2
matched_sessions: 1870
sessions_with_token_delta: 43 (2.3%)
avg_latency_delta_ms: +3.6
kv_hit_rate_baseline: 0.62
kv_hit_rate_new: 0.58
notes: most token deltas are in long-tail sessions >1024 tokens
```
ajay: +3.6ms avg is small but the percent of sessions with token deltas is concerning. do we know if deltas correlate with specific kernels (attention kernel swap)?
samir: profiling hooks will annotate kernel decisions per step. add --emit-trace-kernels to playback so we can map diffs to kernel switches. also capture kernel execution times.
benchbot: submitted runs; first batch (seed 42) finished: artifacts: /bench/exp-20260317-01/seed-42/{out.json,profile.pb,kvlog.txt,checker.txt}
noah: I pulled checker.txt for seed-42: matched_sessions 372, token_delta_sessions 6 (1.6%), avg_latency_delta_ms +5.8, median 1.2ms. kv_hit_rate new=0.55 baseline=0.61.
maria: interesting median tiny but mean higher — a few sessions spiking. can we link spikes to kernel fallback or eviction storms?
samir: kvlog.txt shows eviction bursts during session starts on new runtime when multiple long sessions start concurrently. our async prefetch batches fill slowly and cause more misses early.
tess: action items: (A) run the same seed but force KV prefill on baseline and new runtime to see if that normalizes hit rates (B) enable kernel-decision debug to correlate spikes with specific kernels (C) run a longer 1% trace sample to check tail behavior.
ajay: i'll kick off prefill experiments and enable kernel debug. will tag runs with 'prefill-true' and 'kernel-debug'.
benchbot: prefill runs queued. expected finish in ~2h for the full 20 partitions. posting interim artifacts to the run dir.
noah: for the statistical checks let's also compute KL divergence on token distributions per-session and aggregate. set threshold 0.05 (to triage).
maria: adding that to checker. also add a flag to scrub any literal tokens in outputs before bloom-signature so privacy is preserved.
samir: reminder: when we compare runtimes across hardware types, ensure kernel-selection is allowed only when architecture matches (AVX512 vs AVX2). mismatched hardware was a silent source of nondeterminism last quarter.
tess: noted. CI-bot, please enforce hardware_tag equality for apples-to-apples comparisons.
ci-bot: enforced: run failed if hardware_tag_A != hardware_tag_B.
tess: great. will sync in 3h with initial numbers and a short write-up. if we see >5% token-delta or >10ms mean regression on 95th, we'll roll back the kernel selection change and open a formal investigation.
ajay: acknowledging. I'll also prepare a small smoke test that flushes KV between every session to validate worst-case coldstart impact.
maria: thanks — I'll start aggregating the artifacts into a shared notebook for triage.
noah: ping me if you want help correlating kernel traces to pprof flamegraphs.
tess: thanks all, closing loop later. :white_check_mark:
